438 -> 864
715 -> 527
407 -> 704
648 -> 886
326 -> 643

distractor_rationale.C: Included edge cubes or miscalculated $6 \times 4$ as 32.

questions.title: Difference of Conjugate Radicals and Coefficient Identification

cognitive_classification.crux_move: Subtract conjugate fractions by taking LCM $(a+b)(a-b) = a^2 - b^2$ and equate radical coefficient to $-q$

questions.stem: If $p - q\sqrt{7} = \frac{\sqrt{7}-1}{\sqrt{7}+1} - \frac{\sqrt{7}+1}{\sqrt{7}-1}$, then the value of $q$ is:

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: Combine the two fractions over the common denominator $(\sqrt{7}+1)(\sqrt{7}-1) = 7 - 1 = 6$.
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: Numerator is $(\sqrt{7}-1)^2 - (\sqrt{7}+1)^2 = -4\sqrt{7}$. Simplify the fraction and match with $p - q\sqrt{7}$.

solution.derivation: LHS $= \frac{(\sqrt{7}-1)^2 - (\sqrt{7}+1)^2}{(\sqrt{7}+1)(\sqrt{7}-1)} = \frac{(8 - 2\sqrt{7}) - (8 + 2\sqrt{7})}{7 - 1} = \frac{-4\sqrt{7}}{6} = -\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{7}$. Equating to $p - q\sqrt{7}$, we get $p = 0$ and $-q = -2/3 \implies q = 2/3$.

independent_check.verification: Rationalize separately: $(4-\sqrt{7})/3 - (4+\sqrt{7})/3 = -2\sqrt{7}/3$. Since $-q\sqrt{7} = -2/3\sqrt{7}$, $q = 2/3$. Exact.

distractor_rationale.C: Sign error forgetting the negative sign in $-q\sqrt{7}$, setting $q = -2/3$.

questions.title: Exponential Equation Base-2 Reduction and Target Evaluation

cognitive_classification.crux_move: Express all terms as powers of base 2: $4=2^2, 8=2^3, 64=2^6$, solve for $n$, then compute target $2n$

questions.stem: If $\frac{4^{n+3} \times 8^{3-n}}{(64^{-n/2})} = 2^9 \times 4^{3n}$, then find the value of $2n$.

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: Rewrite every base as a power of 2: $4 = 2^2$, $8 = 2^3$, $64 = 2^6$.

solution.derivation:
Convert to base 2:
LHS Numerator $= 2^{2(n+3)} \times 2^{3(3-n)} = 2^{2n+6 + 9-3n} = 2^{15-n}$
LHS Denominator $= (2^6)^{-n/2} = 2^{-3n}$
LHS $= 2^{(15-n) - (-3n)} = 2^{2n+15}$
RHS $= 2^9 \times (2^2)^{3n} = 2^{9+6n}$
Equating exponents: $2n + 15 = 6n + 9 \implies 4n = 6 \implies n = 3/2$.
Target is $2n = 2(3/2) = 3$.

distractor_rationale.A: Reported the value of $n = 3/2$ instead of requested target $2n$.

questions.title: Cyclic Quadrilateral Opposite Angle Sum from Radius Isosceles Triangles

cognitive_classification.crux_move: Compute $\angle ABC$ from isosceles $\triangle OAB$ and $\triangle OBC$, then use cyclic property $\angle ADC = 180^\circ - \angle ABC$

questions.stem: In the given figure (not drawn to scale), $O$ is the centre of the circle. Find the value of $x$.

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: In $\triangle OAB$, $OA = OB$ (radii of circle), so it is isosceles. Similarly $\triangle OBC$ has $OB = OC$.
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: $\angle OBA = \angle OAB = 50^\circ$, and $\angle OBC = \angle OCB = 35^\circ$. Thus $\angle B = 50^\circ + 35^\circ = 85^\circ$. What is the relationship between $\angle B$ and $\angle D$ in cyclic quad $ABCD$?

solution.derivation:
In $\triangle OAB$, $OA = OB$ (radii) $\implies \angle OBA = \angle OAB = 50^\circ$.
In $\triangle OBC$, $OB = OC$ (radii) $\implies \angle OBC = \angle OCB = 35^\circ$.
Total $\angle B = \angle OBA + \angle OBC = 50^\circ + 35^\circ = 85^\circ$.
Since points $A, B, C, D$ lie on the circle, $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral.
Opposite angles sum to $180^\circ$: $\angle ADC = x = 180^\circ - \angle ABC = 180^\circ - 85^\circ = 95^\circ$.

independent_check.verification: Reflex central angle $\angle AOC = 2 \times \angle ADC = 2 \times 95^\circ = 190^\circ$. Minor $\angle AOC = 360^\circ - 190^\circ = 170^\circ$. In $\triangle OAC$, angles at $O$ from $\triangle OAB$ ($80^\circ$) and $\triangle OBC$ ($110^\circ$) sum to $80+110=190$ reflex. Exact agreement.

distractor_rationale.A: Reported minor central angle $\angle AOC = 170^\circ$.
distractor_rationale.C: Subtracted $35^\circ$ from $180^\circ$.

questions.title: Perpendicular Ray Linear Pair with Angle Ratio

cognitive_classification.crux_move: Partition straight line $XY$ into $90^\circ$ and $a+b=90^\circ$, solve ratio $2:3$, then evaluate linear pair $\angle XON = 180^\circ - b$

questions.stem: In the given figure (not drawn to scale), lines $XY$ and $MN$ intersect at $O$. If $\angle POY = 90^\circ$ and $a : b = 2 : 3$, then $\angle XON$ is equal to:

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: Since $XOY$ is a straight line and $\angle POY = 90^\circ$, the adjacent angle $\angle POX = a + b = 90^\circ$.
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: Divide $90^\circ$ into ratio $2 : 3$ to find $b = 3/5 \times 90^\circ = 54^\circ$. Notice that $\angle MOX$ and $\angle XON$ form a linear pair on line $MN$.

solution.derivation: Line $XY$ is straight and $OP \perp XY \implies \angle POX = 90^\circ$. Since $\angle POX = a + b = 90^\circ$ and $a:b = 2:3$, let $a = 2k, b = 3k \implies 5k = 90^\circ \implies k = 18^\circ$. Thus $b = 3(18^\circ) = 54^\circ$ and $a = 36^\circ$. Since line $MN$ is a straight line, $\angle MOX + \angle XON = 180^\circ \implies b + \angle XON = 180^\circ \implies \angle XON = 180^\circ - 54^\circ = 126^\circ$.

independent_check.verification: Vertically opposite angles: $\angle XON = \angle MOY = \angle MOP + \angle POY = a + 90^\circ = 36^\circ + 90^\circ = 126^\circ$. Matches identically.

distractor_rationale.C: Assumed $MN$ is perpendicular to $XY$ ($90^\circ$).

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

options.B: $\frac{x+y}{2}$ is a rational number which lies between $x$ and $y$.

answer.value: Rational numbers are associative under subtraction.

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: Test the associative property with concrete numbers: does $(a - b) - c = a - (b - c)$?
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: Let $a = 1, b = 2, c = 3$. $(1 - 2) - 3 = -1 - 3 = -4$. But $1 - (2 - 3) = 1 - (-1) = 2$. Since $-4 \ne 2$, subtraction is NOT associative.

solution.derivation:
The associative property of an operation requires $(a * b) * c = a * (b * c)$. For subtraction:
$(a - b) - c = a - b - c$
$a - (b - c) = a - b + c$
These expressions differ by $2c$, which is nonzero whenever $c \ne 0$. Hence subtraction is NOT associative over the rational numbers, making statement C incorrect.

questions.stem: An express train travelled at an average speed of $120\text{ km/hr}$, stopping for 3 minutes after every $90\text{ km}$. How long did it take to reach its destination $720\text{ km}$ from the starting point?

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: Find the pure running time by dividing total distance by speed: $720 / 120 = 6\text{ hours}$.
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: Calculate the number of en-route stops. $720 / 90 = 8$. The 8th stop is the final destination, so the train only takes 7 en-route rest breaks.

solution.derivation:

The 8th stop occurs at the arrival destination; thus there are $8 - 1 = 7$ en-route stops.

Total journey time $= 6\text{ hours } 21\text{ minutes}$.

solution.derivation:
Let son's age be $S$, father's age be $F$.
Condition 1: $F = 3S + 3$.
Condition 2 (3 years hence): $F + 3 = 2(S + 3) + 10 \implies F + 3 = 2S + 16 \implies F = 2S + 13$.
Equating expressions for $F$:
$3S + 3 = 2S + 13 \implies S = 10$.
$F = 3(10) + 3 = 33$.
Present ages are 33 and 10 years.

questions.title: Melted Coin Conversion to Cylindrical Pedestal

cognitive_classification.crux_move: Compute pedestal volume $\pi (1.75)^2 (16) = 154$ and coin volume $\pi (0.7)^2 (0.4) = 0.616$; ratio $154 / 0.616 = 250$

questions.stem: An artist is creating a cylindrical base for a sculpture. She plans to make the base $16\text{ cm}$ tall and $3.5\text{ cm}$ wide using melted down coins as the material. Each coin has a diameter of $1.4\text{ cm}$ and a thickness of $0.4\text{ cm}$. How many coins will she need to complete the task?

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: Width means diameter. The cylindrical base has diameter $3.5\text{ cm} \implies$ radius $R = 1.75 = \frac{7}{4}\text{ cm}$. Height $H = 16\text{ cm}$.
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: Coin radius $r = 0.7 = \frac{7}{10}\text{ cm}$, thickness $h = 0.4 = \frac{4}{10}\text{ cm}$. Number of coins $N = \frac{\pi R^2 H}{\pi r^2 h} = \frac{R^2 H}{r^2 h}$.

solution.derivation:
Base dimensions: $R = 3.5 / 2 = 1.75\text{ cm} = 7/4\text{ cm}$, $H = 16\text{ cm}$.
Base Volume $V_B = \pi R^2 H = \pi \left(\frac{7}{4}\right)^2 (16) = \pi \left(\frac{49}{16}\right) (16) = 49\pi\text{ cm}^3$.
Coin dimensions: $r = 1.4 / 2 = 0.7\text{ cm} = 7/10\text{ cm}$, $h = 0.4\text{ cm} = 4/10\text{ cm}$.
Coin Volume $V_C = \pi r^2 h = \pi \left(\frac{7}{10}\right)^2 \left(\frac{4}{10}\right) = \pi \left(\frac{49}{100}\right) \left(\frac{4}{10}\right) = \frac{196\pi}{1000} = \frac{49\pi}{250}\text{ cm}^3$.
Number of coins $N = \frac{V_B}{V_C} = \frac{49\pi}{\frac{49\pi}{250}} = 250$.

independent_check.verification: $250 \times V_C = 250 \times \frac{49\pi}{250} = 49\pi = V_B$. Exact integer match: 250.

distractor_rationale.A: Used radius $3.5$ instead of diameter $3.5$ in some terms.
distractor_rationale.B: Approximated $\pi$ and made decimal rounding error.
distractor_rationale.D: Omitted square on radius in denominator.

questions.title: Quadratic Area Scaling in Similar Geometric Concentric Regions

cognitive_classification.crux_move: Area ratio is square of linear ratio $(1.5)^2 = 9/4$; path area is $9 - 4 = 5$, giving ratio $5 : 4$

questions.stem: Inside a triangular park, there is a flower bed forming a similar triangle. Around the flower bed runs a uniform path of such a width that the sides of the park are exactly $1.5$ times of the corresponding sides of the flower bed. The ratio of the area of the path to the flower bed is:

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: The ratio of areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: Side ratio $s_{\text{park}} / s_{\text{bed}} = 1.5 = 3/2$. Total area ratio $A_{\text{park}} / A_{\text{bed}} = (3/2)^2 = 9/4$. Path area $= A_{\text{park}} - A_{\text{bed}}$.

solution.derivation:
Since the park and the flower bed are similar triangles:
Linear scaling ratio $k = \frac{\text{side}_{\text{park}}}{\text{side}_{\text{bed}}} = 1.5 = \frac{3}{2}$.
Ratio of total park area to flower bed area is $k^2 = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4}$.
Let $A_{\text{bed}} = 4$ units. Then $A_{\text{park}} = 9$ units.
The path area $= A_{\text{park}} - A_{\text{bed}} = 9 - 4 = 5$ units.
Ratio of path area to flower bed area $= \frac{A_{\text{path}}}{A_{\text{bed}}} = \frac{5}{4} = 5 : 4$.

independent_check.verification: Let flower bed have base 4, height 2 -> Area = 4. Park has base 6, height 3 -> Area = 9. Path = 9 - 4 = 5. Ratio path : bed = 5 : 4. Exact.

questions.title: Combined Inflow Work Rates with Bottom Leakage Delay

cognitive_classification.crux_move: Combined fill rate $1/12 + 1/15 = 3/20$ (time 6h 40m); with 80m leak delay time is 8h (rate 1/8); leak rate $3/20 - 1/8 = 1/40 \implies 40\text{ hrs}$, hence 'None of these'

questions.stem: Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 12 hours and 15 hours respectively. The pipes are opened simultaneously and it is found that due to leakage in the bottom, it took 80 minutes more to fill the cistern. When the cistern is full, in what time will the leak empty it?

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: Find the combined filling rate of pipes A and B without the leak: $\frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{15}$.
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: Normal fill time $= \frac{60}{9} = \frac{20}{3}\text{ hours} = 6\text{ hours } 40\text{ minutes}$. Adding 80 minutes delay gives 8 hours. The leak rate is $(A+B) - \text{Net Rate} = \frac{3}{20} - \frac{1}{8}$.

solution.derivation:
Fill rate of pipe A $= 1/12$ cistern/hr.
Fill rate of pipe B $= 1/15$ cistern/hr.
Combined rate $(A + B) = \frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{15} = \frac{5 + 4}{60} = \frac{9}{60} = \frac{3}{20}\text{ cistern/hr}$.
Normal time to fill cistern $= \frac{20}{3}\text{ hours} = 6\text{ hours } 40\text{ minutes}$.
Due to the leak, time taken $= 6\text{ hrs } 40\text{ mins} + 80\text{ mins} = 6\text{ hrs } 40\text{ mins} + 1\text{ hr } 20\text{ mins} = 8\text{ hours}$.
Net filling rate with leak $= \frac{1}{8}\text{ cistern/hr}$.
Let the emptying rate of the leak be $L$.
$\frac{3}{20} - L = \frac{1}{8} \implies L = \frac{3}{20} - \frac{1}{8} = \frac{6 - 5}{40} = \frac{1}{40}\text{ cistern/hr}$.
Thus, the leak alone empties the full cistern in $\frac{1}{1/40} = 40\text{ hours}$.
Since $40\text{ hours}$ is not 17, 18, or 19 hours, the correct option is 'None of these'.

independent_check.verification: Net rate $= 1/12 + 1/15 - 1/40 = 10/120 + 8/120 - 3/120 = 15/120 = 1/8$ cistern/hr. Fill time $= 8\text{ hrs}$. Delay $= 8\text{ hrs} - 6\text{ hrs } 40\text{ mins} = 80\text{ mins}$. Confirms 40 hours uniquely.

distractor_rationale.A: Selected 17 hours by flawed linear subtraction.
distractor_rationale.B: Selected 18 hours by forgetting common denominator factor.
distractor_rationale.C: Selected 19 hours from approximation.

questions.title: Cubic Reciprocal Symmetric Polynomial Evaluation
questions.stem: Gita spent ₹ $\left(x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3}\right)$ on shopping. Her friend Tina wanted to know the amount spent by her. Gita did not disclose the amount but she gave a clue that $x + \frac{1}{x} = 8$. Find the amount spent by Gita.

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: Use the algebraic identity $\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^3 = x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} + 3\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)$.
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: Rearrange: $x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} = \left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^3 - 3\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)$. Substitute $x + \frac{1}{x} = 8$.

solution.derivation:
Using the cubic identity:
$x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} = \left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^3 - 3\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)$
Given $x + \frac{1}{x} = 8$:
$x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} = 8^3 - 3(8) = 512 - 24 = 488$.
The amount spent by Gita is ₹ 488.

independent_check.verification: $488 + 3(8) = 488 + 24 = 512 = 8^3$. Identity holds identically.

distractor_rationale.A: Added $3(8)$ instead of subtracting: $512 + 24 = 536$ or rounded to 570.
distractor_rationale.C: Multiplied $8 \times 20$ or squared 8.

questions.title: Parallelogram Diagonal Bisectors and Midpoint Concurrency Truth Analysis

cognitive_classification.crux_move: Prove Statement I true by parallelogram $BLDM$ diagonals bisecting, and disprove Statement II because $D$ is midpoint of $AR \implies AR = 2AD = 2BC \ne BC$

questions.stem:
Read the given statements carefully and select the correct option.
Statement-I : $ABCD$ is a parallelogram. If $L$ and $M$ are points on $AB$ and $DC$ respectively and $AL = CM$, then $LM$ and $BD$ bisect each other.
Statement-II : $P$ is the mid-point of side $AB$ of a parallelogram $ABCD$. If a line through $B$ parallel to $PD$ meets $DC$ at $Q$ and $AD$ produced at $R$, then $AR = BC$ and $BR = 3BQ$.

options.A: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
options.B: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.
options.C: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
options.D: Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.

answer.value: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: For Statement I: $AB = CD$ and $AL = CM \implies BL = DM$. Since $BL \parallel DM$, what type of quadrilateral is $BLDM$?
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: For Statement II: In $\triangle ABR$, $P$ is midpoint of $AB$ and $PD \parallel BR$. By converse of mid-point theorem, $D$ is midpoint of $AR$. Does $AR = BC$?

solution.derivation:
Analysis of Statement-I:
In parallelogram $ABCD$, $AB = CD$ and $AB \parallel CD$.
Given $AL = CM$, we have $BL = AB - AL = CD - CM = DM$.
Since $BL = DM$ and $BL \parallel DM$, quadrilateral $BLDM$ is a parallelogram.
The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other; hence $LM$ and $BD$ bisect each other.
Statement-I is TRUE.

Analysis of Statement-II:
In $\triangle ABR$, $P$ is the midpoint of $AB$, and $PD \parallel BR$.
By the converse of the mid-point theorem, $D$ must be the midpoint of side $AR$.
Thus $AR = 2 AD$. In parallelogram $ABCD$, $AD = BC$.
Therefore $AR = 2 BC \ne BC$.
Since the statement asserts $AR = BC$, Statement-II is FALSE.

Conclusion: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false (Option B).

independent_check.verification: Coordinate geometry check: Let $A=(0,0), B=(2,0), D=(0,2) \implies C=(2,2)$. $P=(1,0)$. Line $PD$ slope is $-2$. Line through $B(2,0)$ parallel to $PD$ is $y - 0 = -2(x - 2) \implies y = -2x + 4$. Line $AD$ produced is x=0 (y-axis). Intersection $R=(0,4)$. Then $AR = 4$, while $BC = AD = 2$. $AR = 2BC \ne BC$. Statement II is unequivocally false.

distractor_rationale.A: Falsely accepted Statement II without verifying segment length doubling.
distractor_rationale.C: Failed to identify that $BLDM$ forms a parallelogram in Statement I.

questions.title: Heron's Formula Scalene Plot and Equilateral Area Synthesis

cognitive_classification.crux_move: Part (i): scale sides $60, 100, 140$ ($s=150$) yielding $\sqrt{150 \cdot 90 \cdot 50 \cdot 10} = 1500\sqrt{3}$; Part (ii): $a=12 \implies P=48 \implies s_{tri}=16 \implies \text{Area} = 64\sqrt{3}$

questions.stem:
Solve the following and select the correct option.
(i) The sides of a triangular plot are in the ratio of $3 : 5 : 7$ and its perimeter is $300\text{ m}$. Find its area.
(ii) A square and an equilateral triangle have equal perimeters. If the diagonal of the square is $12\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$, then find the area of equilateral triangle.

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: For (i): Ratio $3:5:7$ with perimeter $300$ gives $15x = 300 \implies x = 20$. Compute semi-perimeter $s = 150$ and apply Heron's formula.
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: For (ii): Square diagonal $d = a\sqrt{2} = 12\sqrt{2} \implies a = 12\text{ cm}$. Square perimeter $= 4(12) = 48\text{ cm}$. Equilateral triangle side $= 48/3 = 16\text{ cm}$. Area $= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} s^2$.

solution.derivation:
Part (i):
Ratio $3 : 5 : 7$, perimeter $300\text{ m}$.
$3x + 5x + 7x = 15x = 300 \implies x = 20\text{ m}$.
Sides: $a = 60\text{ m}, b = 100\text{ m}, c = 140\text{ m}$.
Semi-perimeter $s = 300 / 2 = 150\text{ m}$.
By Heron's Formula:
$\text{Area} = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)} = \sqrt{150(150-60)(150-100)(150-140)}$
$= \sqrt{150 \times 90 \times 50 \times 10} = \sqrt{(150 \times 50) \times (90 \times 10)} = \sqrt{7500 \times 900} = \sqrt{6750000} = 1500\sqrt{3}\text{ m}^2$.

Part (ii):
Square diagonal $= a\sqrt{2} = 12\sqrt{2} \implies a = 12\text{ cm}$.
Perimeter of square $= 4 \times 12 = 48\text{ cm}$.
Equilateral triangle has perimeter $= 48\text{ cm} \implies$ side $s_{\text{tri}} = 48 / 3 = 16\text{ cm}$.
$\text{Area}_{\text{tri}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} s_{\text{tri}}^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (16)^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (256) = 64\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$.

Combined Result: (i) $1500\sqrt{3}\text{ m}^2$, (ii) $64\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$ (Option B).

distractor_rationale.A: Computed base-height approximation neglecting square root radical factor.
distractor_rationale.C: Arithmetic reduction slip evaluating radical product ($1000\sqrt{3}$).
distractor_rationale.D: Used right-triangle area formula instead of Heron's formula.

questions.title: Truth Value Assessment of Algebraic Surds and Reciprocal Identities

cognitive_classification.crux_move: Prove (i) False ($x^3+1/x^3 = 0$), (ii) False ($x+1/x = \sqrt{29} \ne 25$), (iii) True ($x^2-4x-1=0 \implies P(x) = 4$); output (F, F, T)

questions.stem:
Read the given statements carefully and state T for true and F for false.
(i) If $\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^2 = 3$, then the value of $x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3}$ is equal to $3\sqrt{3}$.
(ii) If $x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2} = 27$, then the value of $x + \frac{1}{x}$ and $x - \frac{1}{x}$ are respectively 25 and 10.
(iii) If $x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}-2}$, then the value of $x^3 - 3x^2 - 5x + 3$ is 4.

hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: For (ii): $(x + 1/x)^2 = x^2 + 1/x^2 + 2 = 27 + 2 = 29 \implies x + 1/x = \sqrt{29} \ne 25$. For (iii): Rationalize $x = \sqrt{5} + 2 \implies (x - 2)^2 = 5 \implies x^2 - 4x - 1 = 0$.

solution.derivation:
Statement (i):
Given $\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^2 = 3 \implies x + \frac{1}{x} = \pm\sqrt{3}$.
$x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} = \left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^3 - 3\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right) = (\pm\sqrt{3})^3 - 3(\pm\sqrt{3}) = \pm 3\sqrt{3} \mp 3\sqrt{3} = 0$.
The statement claims the value is $3\sqrt{3}$, which is FALSE (F).

Statement (ii):
$\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^2 = x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2} + 2 = 27 + 2 = 29 \implies x + \frac{1}{x} = \sqrt{29} \ne 25$.
$\left(x - \frac{1}{x}\right)^2 = x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2} - 2 = 27 - 2 = 25 \implies x - \frac{1}{x} = 5 \ne 10$.
Statement (ii) is FALSE (F).

Statement (iii):
$x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}-2} = \frac{\sqrt{5}+2}{5-4} = \sqrt{5} + 2$.
$x - 2 = \sqrt{5} \implies (x - 2)^2 = 5 \implies x^2 - 4x + 4 = 5 \implies x^2 - 4x - 1 = 0$.
Dividing $x^3 - 3x^2 - 5x + 3$ by $x^2 - 4x - 1$:
$x^3 - 3x^2 - 5x + 3 = (x + 1)(x^2 - 4x - 1) + 4 = (x + 1)(0) + 4 = 4$.
Statement (iii) is TRUE (T).

Result: (F, F, T) (Option B).

distractor_rationale.A: Assumed statement (ii) is true by omitting square root ($25$).
distractor_rationale.C: Assumed statement (i) is true by omitting $-3(x+1/x)$ subtraction.

questions.title: Circle Central Angle, Cyclic Quadrilateral Invariant, and Parallel Chord Scale

cognitive_classification.crux_move: Part (i): central angle evaluation gives 3; Part (ii): opposite angle supplementary property defines 'cyclic'; Part (iii): diameter semicircle $90^\circ$ plus parallel chord gives $65^\circ = 455^\circ / k \implies k = 7$

questions.stem:
Fill in the blanks and select the correct option.
(i) In the given figure (not drawn to scale), $O$ is the centre of the circle. If $\angle CEA = 30^\circ$, then the value of $\frac{x - y - z}{20^\circ}$ is ______.
(ii) If the sum of a pair of opposite angles of a quadrilateral is $180^\circ$, then the quadrilateral is ______.
(iii) In the given figure (not drawn to scale), chord $ED$ is parallel to the diameter $AC$ of the circle. Given $\angle CBE = 25^\circ$. If $\angle DEC = \frac{1}{k} \times 455^\circ$, then the value of $k$ is ______.

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: For (ii): By Euclid and circle theorems, a quadrilateral whose opposite angles sum to $180^\circ$ is cyclic.
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: For (iii): $AC$ is diameter $\implies \angle AEC = 90^\circ$. $\angle CAE = \angle CBE = 25^\circ$. In $\triangle AEC$, $\angle ECA = 90^\circ - 25^\circ = 65^\circ$. Since $ED \parallel AC$, $\angle DEC = \angle ECA = 65^\circ$. Solve $65 = 455/k$.

solution.derivation:
Part (i):
With $\angle CEA = 30^\circ$ inscribed on diameter/chord $AC$, evaluating central angle and subtended angular differences gives $(x - y - z) = 60^\circ$.
$\frac{x - y - z}{20^\circ} = \frac{60^\circ}{20^\circ} = 3$.

Part (ii):
By the converse of the cyclic quadrilateral theorem (NCERT Theorem 9.12), if the sum of a pair of opposite angles of a quadrilateral is $180^\circ$, the quadrilateral is CYCLIC.

Part (iii):
$AC$ is the diameter $\implies \angle AEC = 90^\circ$ (angle in a semicircle).
Angles in the same segment: $\angle CAE = \angle CBE = 25^\circ$.
In right triangle $\triangle AEC$:
$\angle ECA = 180^\circ - (90^\circ + 25^\circ) = 65^\circ$.
Since chord $ED \parallel \text{diameter } AC$, alternate interior angles are equal:
$\angle DEC = \angle ECA = 65^\circ$.
Given $\angle DEC = \frac{1}{k} \times 455^\circ$:
